absent: Debugger command execution, breakpoint installation, pager behavior, inter-CPU rendezvous, keyboard entry, crash handoff and remote-debug transition mechanics beyond flag names.
Semantics of fault-tolerant copy primitives, bad-address status encoding, diagnostic output path, and state accessor macros.
Lower-level contiguous allocator behavior, page isolation and migration interaction, numeric alignment and capacity bounds, and architecture fixup effects.
Device DMA mask and limit semantics, coherent mapping cache attributes, reserved-memory framework lifecycle, and cached reservation-pool ownership on detach.
Concurrency rules for area registries and global pool pointers beyond the per-pool lock, and numeric error-code values.

findings.text: A kernel symbol record pairs a numeric address with module attribution and address bounds, section attribution and address bounds, and full symbol attribution and address bounds for version-qualified names.
A breakpoint slot records the address under control together with availability, activation, installation and deferred-handling markers, a compact hardware-type selector, and a hardware length value.

A coherent DMA pool descriptor combines a CPU-visible base with a device-visible base, a frame-number base, a page-count extent, a page-use bitmap, a dedicated lock, and a mode selector controlling how the device base is derived.
Reserved-memory glue for DMA pools is organized as a triplet of callbacks covering early node validation, per-device attachment, and per-device detachment.

Debugger per-CPU control state is a bitmask distinguishing inside-debugger presence, exit in progress, command execution, debugger ownership, forced hold, single-step activity and its breakpoint follow-up, legitimate reentry and recursion, diagnostic suppression, pager readiness, multiprocessor resume handoff and remote rendezvous wait, adjusted resume address, single-CPU release, keyboard entry, crash-image handoff, remote-debug entry and its transition phase, with the upper byte reserved for architecture needs.
Trap classification separates a genuine breakpoint report from a single-step report, a single step taken over an installed breakpoint, and a spurious breakpoint report with no associated breakpoint.
Debugger breakpoint capacity is fixed at sixteen slots.
Debugger pattern search uses a two-hundred fifty-six byte pattern area and a single high flag bit to indicate search handling.

Symbol display options are single-bit requests for surrounding spacing, parentheses, numeric value emission, size emission and line termination, with the default combining value emission and parentheses.

The debugger build assumes eight bytes per word, derives its word-size notion from the width of the native unsigned long type, and chooses non-blocking allocation while the debugger owns the machine and blocking allocation otherwise.

Numeric renderings for debugger addresses use hexadecimal with a radix prefix, providing both compact and fixed-width zero-filled styles for machine and virtual quantities, with separate narrower integer styles for firmware addresses and frame counts.

Debugger memory read and write helpers transfer sized regions between debugger storage and kernel addresses through fault-tolerant copy primitives; a transient suppression marker ensures only one bad-address diagnostic appears across repeated failures until a successful transfer clears it, with failures mapped to a debugger bad-address status.
Symbol-name rendering keeps two fixed-capacity buffers sized for the longest kernel symbol name plus termination, preserving current and previous spellings.

A coherent pool is created from a physical range, device address and byte length, then bound to at most one device; binding refuses absent devices and already-bound devices, teardown releases mapping, bitmap and descriptor state and clears the device link, and declaration failure discards a freshly built pool.
Each coherent pool serializes bitmap allocation and release with its own interrupt-saving spinlock, held only around size validation, region search or release and handle computation.

Allocation from a bound or global coherent pool refuses requests larger than the pool, locates a suitably aligned free extent in the bitmap, derives device and CPU addresses by page offset from the pool bases, returns zeroed storage on success and a null indicator when the pool is missing or exhausted, with a per-device wrapper distinguishing missing pools from attempted allocations.

Release validates that the supplied CPU address lies inside the owning pool extent, translates it to a page index, frees the corresponding bitmap extent under lock, and reports whether the address belonged to that pool, with thin wrappers selecting the per-device or global pool.

Mapping validates that the requested CPU range lies wholly inside the owning pool, checks the caller page window against the allocation length, maps the corresponding frame range with the caller protections, and reports mapping-window errors through an out parameter while indicating pool ownership separately, with wrappers for per-device and global pools.

Device-handle computation either reuses the stored device base or recomputes it from the pool frame base through the platform DMA translation when offset mode is enabled; pool lookup yields null for devices without an attached pool.

Early reserved-memory handling validates device-tree nodes by rejecting reusable regions and recording a designated default-pool region with duplicate definition warnings, per-device attachment lazily creates and caches a pool from the reservation while warning when the reservation exceeds the device DMA range, detachment only clears the device link, and global-pool startup fails when no default reservation was recorded.

Contiguous-area management keeps an ordered registry with a live count, rejects insertion beyond capacity, returns null for out-of-range index queries, and resolves the effective area for a device as its private area when present and the global default otherwise.

Early boot handling parses size with optional base and upper bound, marks fixed placement when the three values meet exactly, accepts per-node sizes and a uniform per-node size with a configured marker, derives percentage-based sizing from total physical memory when enabled, creates the global default area once with build-policy size selection and queues it with a warning on queue failure, then attempts per-node reservations while skipping offline nodes, delegating creation to the lower allocator followed by an architecture fixup that performs no work in these fragments.

Contiguous allocation clamps requested alignment to a build maximum, requires a sleeping-capable allocation context, prefers a device-private area, bypasses small requests without one, then tries a node-local area unless restricted DMA zones are requested before falling back to the global default, returning null when no area can satisfy the request; release forwards to the effective area for the device.

Contiguous-memory diagnostics use a short CMA tag prefix, the default megabyte size comes from build configuration or zero when unset, and byte sizing is expressed as megabytes scaled by one mebibyte.

Coherent and contiguous paths fail safely on invalid sizes, missing mappings, exhausted pools, busy devices, oversized requests, out-of-window mappings, full registries, offline NUMA targets and missing default areas, using null returns, ownership indicators, logged diagnostics and propagated error codes rather than partial updates.

The global coherent pool pointer is write-protected after early init, default reservation base and size live in early-init storage, and contiguous state keeps a single global default pointer plus a per-node pointer table with early-init size and configuration markers.
